correctness.rationale: For every r,h>0 the shadow is exactly an ellipse of semiaxes r,r|U_z| Minkowski-added to an axial segment of length h sqrt(1-|U_z|^2); this yields A=pi r^2 x+2rh sqrt(1-x^2) and P=4r E(1-x^2)+2h sqrt(1-x^2). The Haar density of x is uniform. Direct integration gives E[xE(1-x^2)]=2/3 and E[E(1-x^2)]=pi^2/8. The mixed moment and covariance polynomial follow by expansion. Its crucial coefficient I has an absolutely convergent hypergeometric series, rational recurrence, and rigorously bounded tail beyond term 144. Independent rational Machin bounds for pi prove C>0.0498, -0.69<B<-0.65 and pi>3.14, so B^2<0.4761<64pi C^2. Consequently the covariance polynomial has positive leading coefficient and negative discriminant, globally strictly positive. Its unique positive vertex is the sharp minimizing aspect ratio. The standalone verify.py reproduces all rational inequalities and separately checks fifteen projected hulls and numerical quadratures. No inference from finite samples to an infinite claim is made.

originality.rationale: The central claim concerns the exact mixed shadow-area/perimeter moment for the full family of right circular cylinders, the strict positive covariance for every aspect ratio, and its unique sharp minimizing ratio. The closest primary paper (Finch 2012) contains the same elliptic integral as a component of a different cube-perimeter second moment: the scalar special-function identity is explicitly NOT claimed new. Finch does not state or imply the cylinder covariance polynomial and minimizer. The second inspected full text concerns unlabeled projection-volume distributions, which do not supply a coupled shadow-perimeter statistic. Actual semantic and exact-name searches found related, not dominating records. A historical equivalent outside the inspected sources remains possible and this is not an independent originality certification.

value.rationale: Area/perimeter correlations of isotropic shadows already exhibit both signs for natural regular polyhedra, as Finch established; determining the sign for a continuous family of nonpolyhedral convex bodies is consequently a motivated geometric-statistics question. The exact cylinder mixed moment reduces a genuinely coupled projection statistic to one classical elliptic integral and yields the nontrivial all-aspect strict sign inequality. At fixed radius the result further determines the UNIQUE sharp minimizing shape at an interior height-to-radius ratio about 1.68127, with strictly positive exact value. The proof of the sign requires a global rational discriminant certificate; none of the marginal Cauchy formulas or previously computed elliptic constant alone gives the theorem. This is a structural inequality and natural extremum in an entire two-parameter geometric family, not an arbitrary slice or table lookup.
